profile.entities: Kajaria Ceramics Ltd (Parent); Joint Venture Plants (Morbi); Adhesive Division
profile.subseg: Wall & Floor Tiles; Bathware (Sanitaryware/Faucets); Tile Adhesives & Chemicals
profile.themes: Morbi Cluster Disruption (Gas Crisis); Input Cost Inflation (Gas/Propane); Market Share Consolidation by Organized Players; Inventory Liquidation

bull_bear.body: Buyback approved to return surplus cash (tax-efficient vs dividends) and improve ROE; Working capital optimization priority (cycle down to 51 days).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Sustained high gas prices impacting demand elasticity; Propane ban permanence for industry; Morbi competitors restarting faster than expected; Geopolitical impact on freight costs (UAE freight up to $4k) hurting export potential.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and opportunistic regarding competitor distress; Cautious on providing specific numerical guidance due to macro volatility; Emphasizes structural advantage of multi-location footprint.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management highlighted that Morbi competitors face a 35-40% cost hike (vs Kajaria's 15-16% price increase) due to lower base prices and higher gas dependency, creating a permanent margin gap; Export market effectively closed for Morbi due to freight spikes ($300 to $4000 to UAE), forcing all supply into domestic market but at uncompetitive prices.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Tiles: INR 1,212 cr (+11% YoY); Bathware: INR 117 cr (+6% YoY); Adhesives: INR 44 cr (+110% YoY). Tiles remain core driver; Adhesives showing high base growth.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gas price surge (INR 47 to INR 84/scm) and propane ban shutting down unorganized Morbi clusters; inability to pass on 35-40% cost increases without losing volume. | Somany Ceramics | beneficiary | High | Multi-location player similar to Kajaria; benefits from same supply vacuum and pricing power in North/West markets. |

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 19.19% (vs 10.01% YoY) due to 12-17% price hikes covering gas inflation; Fuel cost mix: North ~INR 62.5/scm (April), South/West ~INR 79-81/scm; Biofuel usage ~15-30% in North spray dryers providing cost arbitrage vs pure gas players.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: No specific guidance given (management cites external volatility); Margin: Targeting 18-19% range; Order Inflow: Momentum positive post-Jan '26, Q1 seasonally weak but YoY April expected strong; Capex/Commissioning: Morbi plants restarted April 16; full capacity running.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A (Inventory-driven model); Finished Goods Inventory reduced by ~1.5 million sqm in March to ~11 million sqm total; Days Sales Inventory improved significantly contributing to 14-day reduction in working capital cycle (51 days).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Market share gain from Morbi unorganized cluster (estimated 150-160 plants running vs 500+ previously); Adhesive segment scaling; Potential for further pricing power as cost differential widens for competitors.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Kajaria leveraged the Morbi cluster shutdown (due to gas shortages) and prior sales unification efforts to drive 11% volume growth and expand EBITDA margins to 19.2% via price hikes, positioning itself to capture significant market share as unorganized competitors face structural cost disadvantages. While Q1 faces transient production lags from the Morbi restart, the medium-term outlook favors consolidated players with multi-location assets and biofuel flexibility.
